mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital for corporations and increases equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals a tight labor market, which typically leads to stronger consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE < 4.5, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in labor market (PAYEMS) and manufacturing activity (INDPRO) indicates a synchronized economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of PAYEMS and INDPRO on SPX returns is not significant (t-test p > 0.05) in any 2-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle, defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 0.5% and increasing by at least 0.2% over the past three months, signals reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS increase > 0.2% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS increase > 0.2% in 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of employment (PAYEMS) reflects strong labor market conditions, which support consumer spending and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1200 thousand units signal robust consumer demand for housing and related sectors, which typically translates into stronger economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST > 1200, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based expansion in consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of RSAFS and HOUST on SPX returns is not significant (t-test p > 0.05) in any 2-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During a manufacturing expansion regime (INDPRO above 105 and rising), industrial output growth supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 105 and rising, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.
